purpose: Controlled vocabulary for the mechanism-fidelity check. Every port's source-leg and port-leg names a primitive { action, target, effect }. The fidelity comparator checks whether source.actionClass === port.actionClass AND source.effectClass === port.effectClass. Verdict: mechanism-coherent if both match; primitive-substituted if either differs; no-source-mechanism if source primitive is null. The two class enumerations below are the load-bearing concept — they define what counts as 'the same primitive'. They are intentionally narrow: ~13 action classes + ~10 effect classes. If a primitive doesn't fit any class, the verdict is ambiguous and gets human review rather than a vibe-grade pass.

re-application.definition: Repeated, controlled re-presentation of a stimulus or signal to the system until the system's response to it changes. The signal is preserved; what changes is the system's response.

blockade.definition: Antagonism or structural inhibition of a signal pathway. The signal cannot act on its target; the target's response is preserved but uncoupled from the signal.

baseline-shift.definition: Tonic modulation of a system's baseline state, changing the reference point from which phasic responses are computed. Long-running, not event-triggered.

stimulation.definition: Phasic activation of a signal pathway, typically time-locked to a target window.

high-frequency-disruption.definition: Sustained high-frequency stimulation that overrides or scrambles a pathological firing pattern. Distinct from stimulation because the target is the pattern, not the message; the goal is disruption.

flooding.definition: Mass uncontrolled injection of resource into a system to override or suppress a signal. Distinct from re-application: signal is not preserved; it is drowned.

forced-reset.definition: External party rewrites a system's setpoint or rule from outside, bypassing the system's own regulatory machinery.
examples: ECT for treatment-resistant depression (in some framings)

window-intervention.definition: Action timed to a specific reactivation or sensitive window in which the system is plastic. The intervention is brief; the timing is essential. Distinct from baseline-shift (continuous) and blockade (continuous-unless-bound).
window-intervention.qualifyingAssertion: A primitive qualifies as window-intervention ONLY IF its outsideWindowAssertion field explicitly states that the action would not produce the named effect outside the plasticity/reactivation window. Mere timing — 'we scheduled this at anniversary because attention is high' — does not qualify. Efficacy must be gated on the window, not merely scheduled within it. Without this field populated, the comparator returns ambiguous, not mechanism-coherent.

parallel-processing.definition: Presentation of input through multiple independent channels simultaneously so processing is distributed rather than single-channel.

restructuring.definition: Reorganization of relationships or connections within a system. The components remain; their wiring changes.

removal.definition: Withdrawal or extraction of an existing input/stimulus/agent.

pre-commitment.definition: Binding the system to a rule-based response that fires automatically when a threshold is crossed, removing discretion at the moment of activation.

restoration.definition: Repair or regeneration of a damaged circuit/structure. Distinct from re-application (which preserves the signal and changes the response) and baseline-shift (which changes the operating point).
restoration.qualifyingAssertion: A primitive qualifies as restoration ONLY IF its repairMechanismAssertion field explicitly characterizes (a) what specific structure or circuit is being repaired AND (b) by what means the repair operates. Unstated mechanisms — 'restore investor confidence', 'repair institutional trust' — do not qualify. This is the class-level catch for the vmPFC failure mode: if no repair mechanism is characterized, the comparator returns ambiguous regardless of whether the source primitive is null.

monitoring.definition: Detection-only intervention that surfaces a signal without acting on it. Diagnostic, not curative.

recalibration.definition: A threshold or setpoint moves to a new value as a result of the action. The system's reference shifts; phasic responses are now computed relative to the new threshold.
examples: risk-pricing threshold recalibration after market re-exposure

attenuation.definition: A signal reduces in amplitude or reactivity. The signal still occurs but with smaller magnitude.
examples: credit-spread reactivity attenuation under tighter regulation

amplification.definition: A signal increases in amplitude or reactivity.

suppression.definition: A signal is blocked, masked, or replaced. Distinct from attenuation: the signal does not get through at all rather than getting through with reduced amplitude.
examples: liquidity flooding suppresses credit panic signal

interference.definition: A process (typically consolidation or learning) is blocked during a specific window. Distinct from suppression: the window is bounded; outside the window the process operates normally.
interference.qualifyingAssertion: A primitive qualifies as interference ONLY IF its targetMustBeActiveAssertion field explicitly names (a) the process being interfered with AND (b) asserts that process must be active/reactivated for the interference to act. Interference with nothing is not interference. If the target process is dormant the action produces no effect; that conditional must be stated, not implied.

redistribution.definition: Allocation of resource or signal changes across the system without net change in total resource.

return-to-prior.definition: System state returns to a previously-established setpoint or baseline. Merges the former 'normalization' (endogenous) and 'reset' (exogenous) classes — they were a collision-shape suspect pair where the only distinguishing axis (agency: who/what does the returning) was already captured by the action class. Forced-reset action → return-to-prior effect = exogenous reset. Baseline-shift or stimulation action → return-to-prior effect = endogenous normalization. The merged effect class does not lose discrimination because action-class match already fires substitution when agency-of-effect differs.
examples: restoration of regulated firing pattern (endogenous via vagal nerve stimulation)
covenant reset to prior debt-service ratio (exogenous via lender action)

merge_record.reason: Collision shape — definitions overlap on 'system returns to baseline'; the discriminator (endogenous vs exogenous) is already captured by action class. Required-field option (force agency declaration on assignment) would not have eliminated collision because authors could honestly write either prose for the same intervention. Merge eliminates the picking-which-class problem entirely; substitution detection at action level handles the cases where agency-of-effect matters.

adaptation.definition: System rewires permanently to a new operating mode in response to repeated input. The system's structure changes, not just its state.
examples: market structural adaptation after repeated parallel-channel disclosure

protection.definition: System insulation from a specific input — the input still exists but cannot reach the target.

mechanism-coherent.definition: Source and port primitives share both actionClass AND effectClass. The transfer preserves the mechanism.
mechanism-coherent.lane_eligibility: Source-verified + mechanism-coherent → grant/SBA/investment lane. Source-real-but-unverified + mechanism-coherent → research/patent lane.

primitive-substituted.definition: Source and port primitives differ on actionClass or effectClass (or both). The port substitutes a different mechanism while claiming transfer. Rejected from all lanes.
primitive-substituted.lane_eligibility: Rejected. Engine output that cites a primitive-substituted residual as a transfer claim has misrepresented the source mechanism.

no-source-mechanism.definition: Source has no extractable structured primitive — either the named intervention does not exist as a clinical protocol, or its mechanism is not characterized in literature. The port may be a real proposal but it is not a transfer.
no-source-mechanism.lane_eligibility: Rejected as a port. May be valid as a standalone hypothesis but cannot claim mechanistic transfer.

ambiguous.definition: Source or port primitive does not cleanly fit any action or effect class in the ontology. Verdict requires human review. Margin case.
ambiguous.lane_eligibility: Held. Operator reviews before lane assignment.

audit_notes: The ontology is intentionally narrow. If it is too narrow, more cases land as ambiguous (held for review) — that is the failure-safe direction. If it is too wide, more cases land as mechanism-coherent — that is the failure-unsafe direction. Bias the ontology toward narrow.
Adding new classes should require evidence that a class genuinely missing — not that an existing class is 'close but not quite'. Close-but-not-quite should be ambiguous.

When an action could plausibly belong to two classes (e.g. window-intervention vs blockade for propranolol-memory-reconsolidation), the more specific class wins. window-intervention is more specific than blockade because it specifies the temporal binding.

The fidelity check makes no claim about EFFICACY — only about COHERENCE. A mechanism-coherent port may still fail in practice; a primitive-substituted port may still produce a desired outcome via a different mechanism. The check rejects mis-labeling, not bad ideas.
